inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 242.127M common shares on the FY2026 10-K cover (dei EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, 2026-07-31) plus 0.35M dilutive RSU/PSU shares (FY2026 diluted 249.373M less basic 249.026M weighted). The 7.56M options outstanding (WAEP $34.23) have zero intrinsic value at the current price and are excluded. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement, ShareBasedCompensation $80.636M (SEC XBRL companyfacts). OpenText does not disclose a separate net-share-settlement tax-withholding outflow; RSUs are settled largely from shares bought by its employee LTIP trust (TreasuryStockValueAcquiredCostMethod $56.2M FY2026, $133.1M FY2025), which is the anti-dilution cash mechanism already represented by expensing SBC with a flat count, so nothing is added on top.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD (10-K, USD functional and reporting currency); OTEX.TO quotes in CAD on the TSX (Yahoo meta currency CAD). All values built in USD and converted to CAD at USD/CAD 1.4254 (Yahoo CAD=X, 2026-10-10T04:21Z). Parity check against the NASDAQ line: OTEX US$23.695 x 1.4254 = C$33.78 vs OTEX.TO C$33.82 observed at the same 2026-10-09 close, a 0.1% tie that confirms rate, direction and quote basis. refresh_price.py does not move this rate; refresh it with the price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST); ERP 5.0%; unlevered enterprise-software beta ~1.0 relevered at market D/E ~1.0 (debt $5.77B vs equity ~US$5.75B) gives equity beta ~1.75 and cost of equity ~13%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.0% (senior notes 3.875-6.9% plus term loan B), 4.5% after tax. 50/50 market weights give ~8.75%; rounded up to 9.0% for refinancing exposure on a 3x-levered roll-up. One WACC across all three scenarios: integration, legacy-erosion and CEO-transition risk are charged in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), naturally under US GAAP: operating lease cost ($71.5M FY2026) sits inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA, so the $202.0M operating lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases ($0.5M) immaterial. lease_cost_pct_path left at zero because the cost is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; flows are attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (routing table row 1: enterprise software operating company; not a bank/REIT/holdco). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model to reconcile. BASIS: unlevered owner FCF (pre-interest, SBC expensed) because net debt is deducted in the bridge; using reported FCF (after $322M interest paid) and also deducting debt would double-count interest. last_fcf here is the contract's reported FCF less SBC ($726.9M, levered); the engine compounds from base_revenue via the component margins, not from last_fcf. MID-CYCLE ANCHOR: FY2026 unlevered owner FCF was ~$968M (18.5% of revenue: 807.5 + 321.7 interest - 80.6 SBC - ~80 interest tax shield) but includes ~$95M of divested eDOCS/Vertica revenue and favourable working capital. FY2027 guidance (FCF $625-725M levered, adj. EBITDA 32-33%, revenue $5.135-5.185B) is the anchor instead: the year-1 component build gives ~$820M unlevered owner FCF (15.9%), equivalent to ~$690M levered company-definition FCF, inside the guide. FY2025 equivalent was ~$846M (16.4%). The modelled EBITDA margin (27.0% year 1) is the company's adjusted EBITDA (32.5% guide midpoint) LESS recurring restructuring/special charges (~$133M FY2026, ~$146M FY2025 - a serial acquirer restructures every year, so these are treated as an operating cost, not a one-off) and other cash leakage, BEFORE SBC (charged separately). D&A is depreciation only (~3%); acquired-intangible amortization ($463M) is excluded so the cash-tax shield is not overstated. Cash tax 25% of EBIT: FY2026 cash taxes paid $300M on a levered basis; unlevered-equivalent ~$380M. BUYBACKS: OpenText is an active repurchaser ($416M FY2026, $413M FY2025, retiring ~5%/yr of shares), far above SBC, so the flat count is funded with room to spare; buybacks are value-neutral in this model. CRA: the up-to-$470M DTA writedown exposure is non-cash and excluded; the residual cash exposure on the FY2012-16 transfer-pricing reassessment is deducted in the equity bridge.

equity_bridge.item: CRA transfer-pricing reassessment, residual cash exposure
equity_bridge.note: Up to ~$78-87M penalties/interest/provincial tax on FY2012-2016 reassessments, ~$32M already provisionally paid (FY2026 10-K tax contingencies note, per Analysis JSON). Deducted at the full residual as a conservative contingent liability; the ~$470M FY2017-2020 exposure is a non-cash DTA writedown and is not a cash claim.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 core revenue growth guide (2-3% cc ex-divestitures), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (5.4%/9.2%) and EPS (66%/18%) CAGRs. None is a usable organic growth rate: book equity is flat because ~$680M/yr goes out in dividends and buybacks; the revenue CAGRs are acquisition-driven (Micro Focus consolidated from Q3 FY2023, then FY2025 fell 10.4%); the EPS CAGRs run from a Micro Focus-depressed FY2023 base. Organic growth has been roughly flat for years; the guided 2-3% core growth is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner (SBC-deducted, levered) series: FY2021 760.4 -> FY2023 525.1 -> FY2026 726.9. The 3-year owner-FCF CAGR (11.5%) runs AHEAD of reported (7.2%) because SBC fell from $130M (FY2023) to $81M (FY2026), the reverse of the usual warning; both start from a FY2023 trough distorted by Micro Focus deal costs and interest. Over five years owner FCF is down 0.9%/yr: the ~$6B Micro Focus acquisition has so far bought revenue but no growth in per-company free cash flow, mostly because interest paid rose from $148M to $322M.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = FY2027 revenue guide midpoint ($5.16B, -1.65% reported after ~$95M of divested revenue). Then core growth of 1.5-2.5%: cloud (~38% of revenue) at high-single digits offsets license and support runoff, the guided 2-3% core rate haircut slightly for a decade-long record of flat organic revenue.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA 32.5% (guide midpoint) less ~5.5pp of restructuring/special and other cash leakage in FY2027, the 'foundation year'; leakage eases to ~3.5pp as the new CEO's reset completes (adj. EBITDA ~33%, restructuring ~1.5% of revenue in perpetuity for a serial acquirer).
base.sbc_rationale: FY2026 1.54%, FY2025 2.03%, FY2024 2.43%; 1.8% flat is the three-year middle. Already low for software, so no further decline is assumed.
base.cap_rationale: 13x terminal owner FCF: a structurally slow, levered roll-up; the 12-15x band for slower businesses. Today's EV is ~12.8x year-1 owner FCF.

scenario_narratives.base: Foundation year then slow compounding. FY2027 lands at the guide midpoint ($5.16B revenue, 32.5% adjusted EBITDA, ~$690M company-definition FCF) as eDOCS and Vertica drop out. Core cloud keeps growing high single digits and roughly outruns the decline in Micro Focus-era license and on-prem support, so total revenue grows 1.5-2.5%. Antoun's reset trims restructuring from ~2.6% to ~1.5% of revenue, so owner margin edges up about 2.5pp. Debt keeps coming down and buybacks keep retiring stock, but neither changes enterprise value. Exit at 13x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The IBM-veteran CEO turns the portfolio. Titanium X / opentext.ai drives cloud attach across the combined OpenText + Micro Focus installed base, cybersecurity and Business Network (EDI) take share, and core growth climbs from 3% to 4.5% instead of fading. With a simpler portfolio and less restructuring, owner EBITDA margin reaches 31.5% (about 34% adjusted). The market then pays 15x for a de-levered, reliably growing information-management franchise.
scenario_narratives.bear: Legacy erosion wins. Hyperscaler bundling (Microsoft 365/SharePoint plus Copilot, Google) and point solutions (Hyland, Box, ServiceNow) hollow out content services outside regulated niches, and aging mainframe/ITOM support runs off faster than cloud can replace it. Revenue shrinks for three years and then grows only 1%. The new CEO's reset becomes another restructuring cycle, owner margin drifts to 25.5%, and with leverage still ~3x EBITDA the multiple compresses to 10x. CRA disputes go against the company.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): net debt is ~2.8x adjusted EBITDA, organic revenue has been roughly flat for a decade, and the CEO has been in the seat six months with FY2027 framed as a reset year. Base 50%: it is the guided path. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs three independent things to go right at once (core growth re-accelerating to 4%+, margin expansion, and a re-rating) for a business that has not grown organically in years.

valuation_philosophy.summary: OpenText is valued as a levered, low-growth cash generator. Value comes from durable recurring revenue (cloud plus support, ~85% of the total) and steady debt paydown, not from growth. The flow is unlevered owner FCF built from guided FY2027 components, charged for recurring restructuring and SBC, so the FY2026 peak (inflated by divested businesses and working capital) is not extrapolated. Debt is deducted once, in the bridge. The price is in CAD; flows and all intermediate values are in USD.
key_risks_to_valuation: Organic decline: if license and support runoff outpaces cloud growth, the base case's 2-2.5% growth is too high. A decade of history supports the bear path as much as the base.
Leverage: $5.77B of debt makes equity a geared residual. A 1x change in the terminal multiple moves equity per share by roughly 5-6%.
Restructuring is a recurring cost here. If the reset adds another multi-year cycle of charges, the margin path is too generous.
CRA tax disputes: only the residual cash exposure is deducted. A loss on the FY2017-2020 depreciable-basis dispute could also raise future cash taxes, not just trigger a non-cash DTA writedown.
Capital allocation: the model treats buybacks as value-neutral. Another debt-funded large acquisition (the company's historic pattern) would change the risk profile and is not modelled.
FX: USD/CAD drives the CAD value one-for-one; a 5% CAD appreciation lowers every CAD figure by ~5% with no change in the business.
